text: Alectinib is a highly potent, second-generation ATP-competitive tyrosine kinase inhibitor that selectively binds to the kinase domain of the Anaplastic Lymphoma Kinase (ALK) protein with nanomolar affinity (IC50 = 1.9 nM). Pathologically, *ALK* chromosomal rearrangements (e.g., *EML4-ALK*) drive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) by creating a constitutively active chimeric fusion protein that triggers oncogenic downstream signaling via the RAS/MAPK, PI3K/Akt, and JAK/STAT pathways. Alectinib inhibits the autophosphorylation of ALK, effectively shutting down these survival and proliferative cascades to induce apoptosis in ALK-dependent tumor cells. Clinically, its exceptional selectivity, high binding affinity, ability to overcome crizotinib-resistance mutations (e.g., L1196M), and superior blood-brain barrier penetration provide a robust therapeutic rationale for its use as a first-line treatment in ALK-positive advanced NSCLC.
